title: Prospective observational study to evaluate urinary Dickkopf-3 (DKK3) as a biomarker for disease monitoring and therapy response in patients with chronic kidney disease receiving SGLT2, RAS and/or aldosterone synthase inhibition
summary:
Background

People with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk of requiring dialysis or dying from heart disease. New research suggests that a specific protein found in urine, called DKK3, may help predict how a kidney disease will progress.

Research Question

This study aims to find out whether the protein DKK3 in urine and blood can help predict the course of kidney disease. It also looks at whether DKK3 levels are linked to other health data, such as heart function or the likelihood of hospital stays.

Methods

This is an observational study. No new treatments are being tested. All participants receive standard medical care for kidney disease. Over several years, urine and blood samples will be collected regularly, along with information about each person’s health—especially kidney and heart function. Hospital stays and other important medical events will also be recorded. The goal is to better understand how kidney disease develops and how it might be treated more effectively in the future.
conditions: The study investigates chronic kidney disease (CKD), a condition with persistently reduced kidney function. It aims to identify biomarkers that can predict disease progression and cardiovascular complications.

interventions.name:
Arm 1: CKD patients receiving SGLT2 and RAS inhibition
Patients with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 20–90 ml/min/1.73 m² and proteinuria) treated with a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor and either an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB).
Study procedures include urine

Arm 2: CKD patients receiving SGLT2 and aldosterone synthase inhibition
Patients treated with an SGLT2 inhibitor and an aldosterone synthase inhibitor (e.g., as part of the EASi-KIDNEY study).
Same assessments as in Arm 1.
Observation period: 24 months.

Arm 3: CKD patients receiving SGLT2, RAS and aldosterone synthase inhibition
Patients receiving triple therapy (SGLT2 inhibitor + RAS blockade + aldosterone synthase inhibitor).
Same assessments as in Arm 1.
Observation period: 24 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Age: Adults aged 18 years or older
	•	Chronic kidney disease with one of the following criteria:
	•	Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) between 20 and 45 ml/min/1.73 m²
or
	•	eGFR between 45 and 90 ml/min/1.73 m² and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) ≥ 200 mg/g
	•	Patients may be on existing treatment with ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs)
	•	Patients may be included regardless of whether they are currently taking an SGLT2 inhibitor
	•	Signed informed consent is required
Exclusion criteria:
Participants will be excluded if any of the following apply:
	•	Age under 18 years
	•	Previous kidney replacement therapy or known dialysis-dependent kidney failure
	•	History of kidney transplantation
	•	Current pregnancy
	•	No written informed consent to participate in the study
